name: Neo4j
does: Graph database; Cypher can be executed over a documented HTTP Query API against self-hosted Neo4j or AuraDB instances.
auth_detail: Basic auth (RFC 7617, username:password base64) is the standard scheme; Bearer tokens via SSO/OIDC providers also supported; AuraDB HTTP API uses the same Basic/Bearer patterns.
gate_detail: Query API enabled by default on Neo4j servers (self-hosted Community/Enterprise free download) or AuraDB instances; AuraDB offers a free-tier instance so a developer gets credentials in minutes without contacting sales.
breadth: Broad - the HTTP Query API accepts arbitrary Cypher, so effectively the whole database is reachable; drivers (Bolt) exist for all major languages.
notes: Fetched all three official pages live. Query API supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, executes Cypher; auth page shows Basic and Bearer headers.

name: Snowflake
does: Cloud data warehouse; SQL API lets you submit SQL statements over REST and poll for results.
auth_detail: Key-pair JWT (RS256, RSA key fingerprint in subject, max 1h validity) or OAuth Bearer tokens (authorization code / client credentials); programmatic access tokens (PAT) also listed.
gate_detail: Requires a Snowflake account (30-day free trial is self-serve); a user/role with the right grants must be set up in the account; key-pair requires generating an RSA keypair and assigning the public key to the user.
breadth: Broad for data - any SQL can run via the API (async submission, results, cancellations); not a full admin/config API surface.
notes: Auth page fetched live confirms key-pair JWT + OAuth (+PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN). Snowflake-managed MCP Server GA in Cortex Agents docs; Snowflake-Labs/mcp repo deprecated pointing to it.

name: MongoDB Atlas
does: Managed MongoDB cloud; Atlas Administration API (REST) manages projects, clusters, users, and (via MCP/drivers) data.
auth_detail: Org/project API keys using HTTP Digest auth with IP access-list requirement; newer alternative is service accounts (OAuth2 client-credentials bearer tokens); both documented on configure-api-access.
gate_detail: Atlas account self-serve with permanently free M0 tier; API keys/service accounts are created by an org or project admin in the Atlas UI/CLI (invited member model, IP allowlist must be set).
breadth: Broad - full Atlas Administration API reference (clusters, network access, users, backups, billing) plus data plane via standard MongoDB drivers.
notes: Admin auth page fetched live: API keys (digest) + IP access list + service accounts. Official MongoDB MCP server (mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server) covers read/write data + Atlas tools.

name: Smartsheet
does: Work-management/spreadsheet SaaS; REST API does full CRUD on sheets, rows, reports, attachments, automations.
auth_detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for third-party apps; API access tokens (Bearer, generated in Smartsheet Developer Tools / account settings) for your own scripts.
gate_detail: Needs a Smartsheet account; access tokens self-generated from the user's account, OAuth apps self-registered; meaningful API use generally requires a paid plan or trial, and org admins can restrict API token management.
breadth: Broad - OpenAPI spec covering sheets, rows, columns, attachments, discussions, reports, users, webhooks, automation.
blocker: API access effectively requires a paid Smartsheet plan (or trial), and no official MCP server could be verified; docs are split between an SPA portal and a deprecated spec site.
notes: Help article fetched live confirms access tokens; redoc.ly spec shell fetched (it self-labels 'DEPRECATED site 2.0.0'). No official/community MCP server surfaced in searches.

name: Harvest
does: Time tracking and invoicing SaaS; API v2 provides full CRUD over time entries, projects, clients, invoices.
auth_detail: OAuth2 authorization-code + refresh tokens for integrations acting on others' accounts, or a Personal Access Token (Bearer in Authorization header) tied to your own user - PATs replaced v1 Basic auth.
gate_detail: Fully self-serve: OAuth2 apps created from the developer settings page, PATs generated from ID settings page for any Harvest account (free trial available).
breadth: Moderate - complete domain coverage (time, expenses, clients, projects, invoicing) with rate limits, but limited to Harvest's own domain.
notes: Auth page and MCP help article both fetched live; MCP article describes connecting Harvest data via MCP for Pro/Premium plans.

name: Brex
does: Corporate cards / spend management platform; Developer API covers accounting, budgets, expenses, payments, team, transactions, travel, webhooks.
auth_detail: Bearer user/API tokens (admin-provisioned from Brex Dashboard > Developer) as Authorization header; OAuth2 for third-party apps and the Brex MCP server (OAuth authorization server accounts-api.brex.com/oauth2/default, supports Dynamic Client Registration).
gate_detail: Must be a Brex customer: an account/card admin must accept the Developer API agreement in Settings > Developer, then tokens are generated there; Brex MCP additionally requires enabling the 'Brex in AI assistants' beta; no open public sandbox for non-customers.
breadth: Broad - nine documented API groups (accounting, budgets, expenses, fields, onboarding, payments, team, transactions, travel) plus webhooks and OpenAPI specs per group.
blocker: Credentials require an existing Brex account where an admin accepts the Developer API agreement - not self-serve for outside developers.
notes: Both pages fetched live. Hosted Brex MCP server at api.brex.com/mcp; OAuth or API-key auth documented.

name: Ramp
does: Spend/finance automation platform; Developer API for cards, bills, accounting sync, transactions, users, plus webhooks and Custom Records.
auth_detail: OAuth 2.0: client-credentials grant (internal server-to-server) or authorization-code + refresh (third-party); token endpoint /developer/v1/token authenticated with HTTP Basic (client_id:client_secret); scope model resource:read/write.
gate_detail: Must be a Ramp customer with admin dashboard access: create a developer app under Company > Developer, pick grant type and scopes, copy client ID/secret; sandbox environment demo-api.ramp.com available but sandbox access is via a request form.
breadth: Broad - full REST surface (cards, bills, payments, accounting, custom records, webhooks) plus an official CLI with agent mode and Agent Cards for agentic checkout.
blocker: Only Ramp customers with admin access can mint API credentials; sandbox requires a separate request.
notes: Ramp ships llms.txt machine-readable docs (fetched live). Official Developer MCP server + account-data MCP (support.ramp.com Ramp MCP guide). Ramp also pushes an AI-agent story: CLI agent mode, Agent Cards.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
does: B2C e-commerce platform; Commerce APIs (B2C Commerce API/SCAPI, OCAPI) for storefront/shopper and admin operations.
auth_detail: SLAS (Shopper Login and API Access Service) issues ShopperToken JWTs (30-min access + refresh) using OAuth 2.1 grants: authorization_code_pkce for registered/guest public clients, client_credentials for private guests, getTrustedSystemAccessToken for trusted systems; SLAS admin tools use Salesforce Account Manager.
gate_detail: Each SLAS tenant is tied to a licensed B2C Commerce instance; SLAS clients are created by admins with the SLAS Organization Administrator role in Account Manager + SLAS Admin UI; guest 'shopper' tokens are free per-request but still need a registered SLAS client; no self-serve path.
breadth: Moderate-to-broad - SCAPI shopper + admin APIs and legacy OCAPI, but auth spans Account Manager, SLAS public/private clients, and tenant setup.
blocker: No self-serve credentials: requires a licensed B2C Commerce instance and admin-provisioned SLAS clients (Account Manager + SLAS Org Admin role); live developer.salesforce.com docs also aggressively bot-block (HTTP 403).
notes: Official SLAS page fetched via Wayback (May 2026 snapshot, 200); live page returns 403 (Akamai). Confirms OAuth 2.1 grant table, guest/registered shopper tokens, Account Manager admin flow.

name: QuickBooks
does: SMB accounting SaaS (QuickBooks Online); Accounting API provides CRUD on ~29 entity types plus reports.
auth_detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with refresh tokens (no per-user API keys); app registered on Intuit Developer portal, connect to a company (realm ID) via browser consent; 100-day refresh-token window.
gate_detail: Free Intuit developer account is self-serve; creating an app and connecting to a sandbox company is easy (localhost redirect URIs accepted in sandbox); production go-live requires a public HTTPS callback and Intuit's production activation process.
breadth: Broad for accounting - entities, queries, batch operations, attachments, reports; Sandbox environment auto-provisioned per developer app.
blocker: Full OAuth app setup + browser handshake required (no simple API key); production apps go through Intuit activation, and refresh tokens lapse after ~100 days.
notes: Intuit portal is a JS SPA (fetched shell 200); official MCP README fetched and confirms OAuth2, sandbox-easy vs production-harder gating. Official Intuit-org MCP server with 145 tools.
